V3-3134 — investigation summary The issue: On some CFN documents (TCC and HedgeServ_MIT on AMERS), the asset_type and vehicle_type columns in the database were coming back NULL instead of FUND and INVESTOR. Root cause — two things stacked together: 1. Parser side: For these specific documents, the parser failed to extract any actual content. The parser output only contained metadata (document type, parsing time, feature flags) but no investor block, no fund block, no payment metrics. I communicated this to and it seems a few days ago there was a big parser update which could've explained the empty parser output for the original document and normal parser output for the second upload of the same renamed document. Also, confirmed there is a parser bug for CFNs which he will fix. 2. Backend side: When the parser returns nothing useful, our code falls back to filling in default metrics using the investor and fund already linked to the document. But the code that built those fallback metrics wasn't setting the entity type — so we ended up saving rows with name and ID but no type. That one missing piece then cascaded into multiple rows because other parts of the code reused that incomplete data to build even more default metrics. Result: - The backend bug will be fixed by explicitly setting FUND as asset type and INVESTOR as vehicle type in the code path that fills in default metrics when the parser returns no content. - The existing bad rows on dev/prod still need a data backfill (either re-parse the affected docs or update the rows directly).

The parser populates type on its own items, but the document's investor/fund are stored as EntityView, which has no type column — so when ensureNetPaymentIsPresent synthesizes a NET_PAYMENT from document.investor / document.fund, name and id come through but type is lost. This fallback only kicks in when the parser output doesn't already provide vehicle/asset on the metrics (i.e. no NET_PAYMENT metric exists and we have to build one); V3-3134 patches the missing type by hardcoding INVESTOR / FUND (the semantic slot tells you what the type must be) behind a flag. It's a narrow fix for a model gap in EntityView rather than a parser bug — the "real" fix would be to add type to EntityView so no downstream code has to re-derive it.
